comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Landed and green through `./dev`.

The CLI moved, not the window: `working` is blue and `done` is green in both now, `blocked` stays yellow in the terminal because the sixteen have no orange, and `idle`/`unknown` stay bare because no colour is what resting looks like in a list of words.

The legend is written down for the first time - `docs/architecture.md` with the reasoning, `docs/cli/window.md` so it ships inside the binary for an agent with no repo - and both source sites now cite the doc and each other, with a test per side that fails if its own row moves.

Considered and rejected: a hue table in `muster-core`. A hue never crosses the seam, so Swift would keep its table and the core would gain a second rather than replace one, plus a `muster-cli` -> `muster-core` edge Cargo.toml deliberately refuses. A text lint across both files is the thing to promote to if a tripwire ever fails to fire.

Open question for you: plain ANSI blue (34) is the least legible of the sixteen on a dark background, and `working` is the state a window spends most of its time in. `BrightBlue` is the same hue slot if it reads badly in your theme.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster window` painted working green and done blue; the window paints working blue and done green. Two independent literals, and no document anywhere stated the legend - so the second author had nothing to disagree with.

Reported as "the dot stays green after an agent finishes": green is `done`, working is blue, but the CLI had taught the opposite.

The CLI moves, because attention lives in the window. Legend written into docs/architecture.md and docs/cli/window.md, each source site citing the doc and the other surface, and a tripwire test per side.
title: 🎨 The window and the CLI paint agent states in inverted colours
